answer: Sybil resistance binds each identity to bonded collateral and links correlated equivocation at detection: if k coordinated identities sign conflicting histories, aggregate slashing grows as O(k^2), not merely k. A swarm therefore cannot cheaply spread risk; detection applies an exponential multiplier to capital loss, while depleted bonds depreciate asymmetrically. The ridge of evidence must be hard to forge, and an onyx ledger records each proven fault.
